provenance.citation: Bellman, R. (1957). Dynamic Programming. Princeton University Press. (Functional equation / principle of optimality, Chapter III; successive-approximation solution, Chapter IV.)
provenance.locus: The functional equation V(s) = max_a [ r(s,a) + γ Σ p(s'|s,a) V(s') ] and its solution by successive approximation (value iteration); closed-form geometric-series fixed points for stationary policies.
provenance.notes: Bellman 1957 provides the method, not a canonical small numeric example; the fixture instantiates a 3-state chain whose optimal values are hand-derivable in closed form from the functional equation: V(goal)=0 (zero-reward self-loop), V(s1)=2 (reward 2 then goal), V(s0)=max(0.1+0.9·V(s0), 0+0.9·V(s1)) = max(1.0, 1.8) = 1.8 — so the optimal action at s0 is 'go', not the myopic 'stay'. The Russell & Norvig 4×3 grid was NOT used because its published utilities assume γ=1, which is outside this breed's documented contract γ ∈ [0,1) (deviation recorded).

input.intent: solve the chain MDP by value iteration (Bellman functional equation)

expected.notes: Hand-derived fixed point of the Bellman functional equation; Bellman residual < 1e-4 at every state.
